key_insight: A scaffold-aware foundation model pretrained on small-molecule natural products combines masked objectives and contrastive learning to produce representations that markedly improve taxonomy classification, genome mining, and virtual screening performance.
problem_solved: Existing molecular foundation models are not optimized for the unique scaffold diversity and taxonomy signals of natural products, limiting discovery workflows that link molecules to biosynthetic origins and biological activity; this work addresses representation gaps to enable more accurate NP-focused analyses.
method: Pretrain a scaffold-aware encoder on a curated corpus of small-molecule natural products.
Use masked modeling objectives to learn chemical context and contrastive loss to align scaffold, taxonomy, and biosynthetic signals in embedding space.
Evaluate and adapt the pretrained model to downstream tasks: taxonomy classification, genome mining (linking BGCs to metabolites), and virtual screening.
impact: Provides an NP-specialized pretrained model that boosts accuracy and data efficiency across discovery tasks, enabling practitioners to accelerate natural-product-driven drug discovery and genome-guided prioritization with transferable embeddings.
visual_elements: Schematic of model: input molecules → scaffold-aware encoder → dual objectives (masked modeling + contrastive learning).

paper_title: Pretraining a foundation model for small-molecule natural products
paper_authors: Yuheng Ding, Bo Qiang, Shaoning Li, Yiran Zhou, Jie Yu
